title: Rewrite multi-join hot paths using partitioned materialized projections to reduce control-plane join costs
creator: Ethan Brooks
description:
Problem: Several control-plane read paths (project/team/usage reporting) execute long multi-table joins that cause p99 latency spikes and high CPU during tenant-heavy queries. These queries contribute to recurring outages in analytics dashboards and slow rollout operations for large customers.

Goal: Replace the most frequently hit multi-join patterns with compact, partitioned materialized projections (MV) and lightweight shadow tables that are kept near-real-time via small transactional backfills. This should reduce per-query CPU and I/O, simplify index maintenance, and provide a safe online migration path with low downtime.

Approach:
- Identify top 10 join patterns by read-cost using existing query telemetry.
- Design partitioned materialized views keyed by tenant_id + date buckets (or project_id where appropriate) and matching the most common predicate shapes.
- Implement MV refresh via incremental delta pipeline: small trigger-based change buffers + scheduled near-real-time compaction jobs.
- Introduce compact covering indexes on the MV to remove expensive joins.
- Provide query layer routing flags (feature-flag) to switch to MV-based read paths per-route.
- Create an online migration plan with safety toggles, double-writes for 2 weeks, and backfill/resync steps.

Success criteria:
- 60-80% reduction in p50/p95 CPU/token for targeted endpoints.
- 40% reduction in observed long-running control-plane read queries.
- No customer-facing incidents during migration; ability to rollback instantly by flipping feature flags.

Risks and mitigation:
- Stale projections: bound staleness to <=30s with rapid delta pipeline and surface staleness metrics.
- Increased storage: use TTL/compaction for older partitions and audit cost.
- Correctness regressions: add end-to-end golden-query comparisons and PRD-run smoke tests.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Week 0-1: Telemetry and query sampling; finalize MV schemas.
2) Week 2-4: Implement MV creation + small-scale delta pipeline; unit tests.
3) Week 5-6: Canary on internal tenant with feature-flag off-by-default; compare results.
4) Week 7-8: Gradual ramp to production with 10% -> 50% -> 100% route switch windows.
5) Week 9-12: Full rollout and post-mortem.

Instrumentation: Add metrics for MV freshness, backfill throughput, per-tenant read latency, and index maintenance durations. Dashboards and alerting to be added to Redwood Console.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Materialized projection exists for top-3 join patterns and passes golden-query parity tests; 2) Feature-flag route switch shows >=60% p95 CPU reduction in canary; 3) Backfill job completes without data drift; 4) Runbook updated and sign-off from SRE and PM.
